title: add-jsonschema-strict-mode-openai-compat
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Add OpenAI-compat structured output using a json_schema-style response_format with a strict validation mode and clearer error semantics so partner customers can rely on deterministic JSON output. This PR implements schema validation at the API surface, improves error messages for schema mismatches, and wires strict-mode behavior into the OpenAI compatibility layer so existing OpenAI-format clients can opt-in via response_format: {type: "json_schema", json_schema: <schema>, strict: true}. Design summary: 1) Add a response_format parser and validator in the API gateway that detects json_schema payloads and compiles validators at request time (with caching). 2) Introduce a strict_mode path: when strict=true we run post-generation validation and, on mismatch, attempt up to one auto-correct pass (guided re-prompt) before returning a structured error that mirrors OpenAI-compatible error fields. 3) Streaming stability: partial streaming is supported while validation runs; if final validation fails we send a final error envelope over the stream and set a clear error_code and error_message. 4) Tool/function-calling compatibility: when response_format targets a function schema, the handler will prefer the function-calling channel if the generated JSON matches the function signature. 5) Error messages: new well-structured error codes (JSON_SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED, JSON_SCHEMA_AUTO_FIX_FAILED) and human-friendly messages with a short validation diff. Implementation notes: gateway changes in server/api/response_format.go and openai compatibility layer updates in openai/compat/handler.go. Validation uses xeipuuv/gojsonschema for server-side checks and fastjson for parsing to keep latency low. Caching: compiled validators are cached keyed by schema fingerprint; cache has LRU with TTL. Rollout plan: feature gated behind ff_json_schema_strict and default off; gradual rollout to 10% of hosted API callers for 48h, monitor validation failure rate and streaming error spikes. Manual QA: added unit and integration tests, including streaming rejection cases and function-calling handoff. Backwards-compatible notes: default behavior is unchanged unless response_format includes json_schema; existing clients unaffected. Checklist: - [x] schema parser and validator implemented - [x] openai compat plumbing added - [x] streaming error envelope implemented - [x] unit/integration tests added - [x] docs and examples updated - [x] feature flag gating and rollout plan documented

review_comments: Alex Chen: Please add more context in the docs about auto-fix semantics and whether the prompt is recorded for privacy/audit - also add a flag to disable auto-fix.

Maya Patel: Added ff_disable_auto_fix flag and documented audit behavior in docs. The re-prompt uses an abstracted deterministic wrapper; we record only the fix outcome not the prompt text by default.
Ravi Singh: CI failed on windows build due to path case in cache.go - please normalize filenames.
Maya Patel: Fixed path normalization in cache.go and added cross-platform unit.
Priya Sharma: Can we keep errors OpenAI-compatible (type, message, param)? Consider adding an HTTP header for validation-error-code so infra can alert.
Maya Patel: Errors now include openai_error_code and we emit X-Redwood-Validation-Error for observability.
changelog_entry: Add json_schema response_format with strict validation mode and OpenAI-compat error semantics. Feature-gated and opt-in via response_format.
note_on_migration: No migration required for existing clients. Opt-in only via response_format. Operator note: enabling strict mode can increase 99th percentile latency due to validation/re-prompt; recommended to monitor validation_failure_rate metric.
